page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is provided via a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core scaling due to the dual-vCPU configuration. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated as average at 2215.58, whereas the multi-core CPU performance falls into the lower percentile at 2263.98. Memory performance is mixed, with an average PassMark memory score of 1927.71, though large-block memory write bandwidth is limited at 12.15 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for specialized vector and matrix operations.

This server configuration presents a clear tradeoff between high memory density per core and limited overall compute parallelism. While database operations and Redis SET benchmarks show weaker relative performance, the instance remains suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. Appropriate workloads include small-scale databases, caching layers, lightweight web serving, and basic text processing or low-demand LLM inference tasks.
